title: High walls
body: A high wall doesn't announce itself before it fails — the Stage 4 crack went from "confirmed" to a 200mm irregular gap needing a 300m exclusion zone and roped-in operators, and the July 9 Block 511 closure shut down an entire face with no warning in the shift handover. Treat every wall as live, not as scenery.
keyPoints: The 10 m exclusion zone from any bench edge is non-negotiable — no one enters without Foreman or Supervisor authorization, full stop.
Walls get inspected before work starts, after every blast, and after every weather event — from both inside the pit and from the top, because a slip can be invisible from one side only.
Loose material within 5 m of a bench edge is a clean-up trigger, not a "get to it later" item — if the excavator can't reach it from above or below, the area gets barricaded immediately.
Machines working near a high wall sit at 90 degrees to the face so they can retreat fast, and operators stay in the cab in designated dangerous areas.
Frozen material against pre-split lines, known slip zones, or fresh dykes mean daylight-only work under full supervision — no exceptions on night shift.
apply: On your walk, cross-check that every wall active this shift has a documented post-blast or post-weather inspection logged — Block 511's July closure showed how fast a face can go from working to shut with zero notice in the handover record.
